entries.subject: Five surveys land, and the app finally explains itself
entries.body:
This wave answered four questions the user asked directly: is everything
working, is it beginner friendly, is there a guide for each section, and is
there an introduction to what ComfyUI can generate. Three are now yes.

WHAT SHIPPED

- studio/capabilities.json + /capabilities: the 92-folder archive under
  claude-generated/ catalogued into 34 capabilities, each with a sample
  chosen by looking at it. The page states the gap plainly - 8 reachable in
  the app, 19 real and unreachable, 13 of those rendered and runnable today.
- studio/guides/ + /guide: 13 plain-language guides, one per section plus
  getting-started and the mental model. Injected into every page nav the
  same additive way /video and /dossier already were.
- TERRA rebuilt on the t2i path. The old sheet was made through the qwen
  edit path, so it transmitted that paths poreless skin into every photoreal
  render of her. The new face panel is born where the skin is real and the
  body panel is generated from it, so both halves are one person.
- Five demo films, 72 beats, 0 unnamed motion holds against 21 of 29 in the
  three older films. The lever was authoring: derive_motion only reads the
  first comma-clause that yields a mover.
- 810 gallery artworks across 57 recipes, every one carrying its full recipe.
- studio/_tools/healthcheck.py and HEALTH.md: a ranked, measured defect list.

WHAT THIS COMMIT REPAIRS

Probing studio/_tools/ with --help made 17 tools run their whole job.
style_verdicts2.py overwrote 10 style cards, replacing measured LoRA-rescue
verdicts with stale stubs and reverting engine routing on three of them.
All 10 are restored from HEAD, verified card by card: verdict text back
(stop_motion_felt 84 chars to 1409), engine back to qwen on comic_halftone,
pointillism and stop_motion_felt, status back to ready on two. The stray
directory literally named --help, holding 66 misplaced style cards, is gone.

Not everything flagged as damage was damage. The deterministic look and
shot_fx cards were reported clobbered; the diff shows they went from 7 looks
to 25 with nothing lost. That was an upgrade and it is kept.

The restore moved the real engine split, so three numbers in the guides were
wrong - they had been measured from the live API during the damaged window.
styles.md and mental-model.md now say 85 anime / 45 qwen and 94 ready /
24 weak / 12 unavailable, re-derived from the API rather than retyped.

healthcheck.py could not see either new feature: its route list predates
them, so it reported clean while testing neither /capabilities nor /guide.
It now checks both, plus /guide/<slug> and the three new APIs.

GROUND TRUTH, NOT TAKEN ON TRUST

Server restarted from source. All 15 pages and all 23 real APIs answer 200
with sane bodies. All 13 guides answer on both /guide/<slug> and
/api/guide/<slug>; a bad slug 404s. Every page carries exactly one guide
link except /changelog, which has no guide mapped. Both agents serve.py
edits survive together and the file parses.

Six pages screenshotted and looked at, plus contact sheets from three
different agents. The TERRA proof shows real skin, freckles and the wardrobe
surviving into a close frame. Agent 5s subject-absence claim reproduces -
several storybook_attic cells are empty attics with no child in them.

check_refs 1925 refs / 0 dangling. lora_scan clean. healthcheck 3 BROKEN,
16 WRONG, all pre-existing and all named in HEALTH.md.

STILL BROKEN, HONESTLY

fx_chain has no branch for dolly_zoom, orbit or rack_focus, so those clips
are byte-identical to static. The night grade clips to black rather than
darkening - measured input luma 48 goes to 0. TERRAs tags still say red hair
ribbon while all 160 renders draw a horned ornament; fixing it needs a new
sheet and a retrain. 17 tools still run their job when handed --help, which
is the defect that caused the damage this commit repairs.

entries.author: sechang11
entries.subject: A photographic reference sheet should be a real character sheet
entries.body:
Three sheets, one seed, one prompt. The body sheet carries the costume correctly - ochre
robe, carmine cape, brown belt - and gives a small soft face, because the qwen edit path
reprojects the sheet and inherits whatever resolution the face had in it. A close portrait
sheet fixes the face and LOSES THE COSTUME: the ochre robe comes back red and the belt
disappears, because the wardrobe was never in the sheet to carry.

The composite - close portrait hstacked with the body image - keeps the costume AND
improves the face. Qwen-Edit conditions on the whole image and takes whatever is legible
in it rather than choosing between them, which is exactly what a physical character sheet
has always been for.

This settles where the photoreal face actually comes from. The character LoRA is
animagine-locked and does nothing on qwen, so every photoreal render of her is this one
image being reprojected into a new scene. No LoRA can improve it because weights are not
in that path at all. Fix the sheet and everything downstream improves.

The first attempt at building the composite failed silently - a bad crop meant the body
panel was never written and the sheet stayed the close portrait, so the cell labelled
COMPOSITE in the first comparison was a duplicate of the close one. Rebuilt, dimensions
checked, and re-rendered before anything was concluded.

entries.author: sechang11
entries.subject: The photoreal face is the same pixel problem, and the sheet is teaching it
entries.body:
Four arms at one seed on the qwen edit path. The current three-quarter-body framing gives
a small soft face - the ugly one. CLOSE FRAMING ALONE fixes it: real skin texture,
catchlight in both eyes, individual hair strands, on the same 7.5 second path with
nothing else changed.

Dropping the Lightning LoRA and running 20 steps at cfg 2.5 is marginally cleaner and
takes 55.8 seconds. Seven times the cost for a difference you have to hunt for. Not worth
it.

The fourth arm rendered the same close prompt with NO reference sheet and produced a good
face belonging to a different woman - which is the sheet doing exactly the job it exists
for, and worth having on the record next to the others.

The consequence lands on the sheet itself. sheet_photo_terra.png is a three-quarter-body
image, so everything conditioned on it inherits a small face. A photographic reference
sheet should be a CLOSE PORTRAIT: the sheet teaches the face, and a sheet whose face is
ninety pixels teaches a ninety-pixel face.

entries.author: sechang11
entries.subject: An ugly face is a pixel problem, not a weights problem
entries.body:
Five arms at one seed, every cell cropped to the same head region at the same display
size so the comparison is about the face rather than about who stood closest to camera.

Full body gives a small soft face with indistinct features - the ugly result. Upper body,
same seed and same LoRA, gives a crisp face with clean eyes and lineart. Raising the
resolution on the same full-body composition recovers much of the difference. Raising the
LoRA from 0.5 to 0.85 changes the face barely at all.

The arithmetic: at 832x1216 in a full-body frame the head is about an eighth of the
height, so the face is roughly 90 pixels, and SDXL samples in an 8x-downsampled latent -
that face was decided by about an 11x11 patch. No LoRA can add detail the sampler never
had room to draw. Terra's own frame_verdict already put the honest cut-off at 5_wide and
most recent sheets were rendered fuller than that.

So the fix order is frame closer, raise resolution, add a face-detail pass - and only
then consider weights.

The fourth arm attempted that detail pass and MY COMPOSITE BROKE IT: the re-rendered crop
came back fine and the feathered paste-back washed it out. That cell is my bug, not a
negative result, and it is stated as such rather than left looking like evidence against
the technique. The primitives for a proper one are on this box - SDPoseFaceBBoxes,
CropByBBoxes and VAEEncodeForInpaint.

entries.author: sechang11
entries.subject: Realism is a ladder, and its two halves take different routes
entries.body:
REAL LIFE is fixed. The qwen edit path through a PHOTOGRAPHIC reference sheet gives real
wool and raw silk, a real stone hall with a real shaft of light, and hair that reads as
hair rather than a wig. The earlier cosplay result is gone.

But the ladder collapsed in the middle. Rungs 1 through 4 came back nearly identical: the
Qwen-Edit reference sheet pins the MEDIUM as hard as it pins the identity, so asking that
path for a 3D animated feature or an oil portrait returns the same photograph. It is the
same suppression IPAdapter does on the anime path, showing up in a new place - and it
means the qwen edit route cannot produce semi-real at all.

SEMI-REAL WORKS ON THE ILLUSTRATION ENGINE instead: the danbooru name plus the trained
LoRA at 0.5 plus a painterly or CG style, with IPAdapter at 0.0. Oil, concept art,
pre-raphaelite and cgi all land as visibly different media and all four hold her headpiece,
hair, bodice, sarong and boots. That is the route for anything between a photograph and a
cel, and it is the opposite engine from where anyone would look for it.

studio/_tools/realism_ladder.py renders the whole spectrum for any character so the rung
can be pointed at rather than argued about.

entries.author: sechang11
entries.subject: The name is load-bearing after all - correcting this card's own claim
entries.body:
This card said the trained LoRA carries Terra with the danbooru name stripped from the
prompt, and therefore that she is a cast member rather than a prompt trick. That was
wrong. It was read off a small column in terra_lora_check.jpg and it was too generous.

The user spotted the real pattern unprompted, on the full-body sheets where it is
unmissable. In costume_ab.jpg rows 1 and 2 are her and rows 3 and 4 are not, and the
variable between those pairs is THE NAME, not the LoRA version: v1 and v2 both hold with
full tags, and both fail without the name. costume_recaptioned.jpg says the same thing
with two rows instead of four.

What is actually true is that the tag and the weights are COMPLEMENTARY, and the tag is
load-bearing. Without the name she becomes a generic green-haired woman in a long gown -
the headpiece, the asymmetric fringed sarong and the bodice all go. The LoRA refines and
stabilises what the name summons rather than replacing it.

So provenance known_partial is sharper than it looked: partial is not a half-measure to
be trained away, it is a permanent dependency on the tag. Keep the danbooru name in every
prompt for her.

entries.author: sechang11
entries.subject: The 0.85 setting collapse was never about strength
entries.body:
This project reported twice, as measured, that a character LoRA at 0.85 destroys the
setting - NIKA's sunlit field became a grey void, and TERRA's snow forest collapsed to
flat beige. Both observations were real. The explanation was wrong.

It was the UNCAPTIONED TAUPE BACKDROP of the turnaround being absorbed into the trigger.
At high strength the LoRA was reproducing its own training background over whatever place
was asked for. Evidence at studio/samples/cast/terra_costume_fix/setting_grid.jpg: the
uncaptioned v1 at 0.85 gives a featureless taupe void for snow_road and reduces a meadow
to an arch-shaped window cut into a wall, while the captioned v3 holds a real forest with
depth and a real meadow AT THE SAME 0.85 AND THE SAME SEED.

So 0.85 is not inherently unsafe and 0.5 was a workaround for a dataset defect rather
than a law. The default stays 0.5, because that is the strength the rest of this
character's evidence was measured at and nothing has shown 0.85 to be BETTER - only that
it is no longer destructive. Overclaiming in the other direction would repeat the mistake.

Recorded on every LoRA-backed character, not just Terra, because any future character
trained from an uncaptioned single-backdrop turnaround inherits the same defect.

entries.author: sechang11
entries.subject: A removal is only fatal when nothing is left named
entries.body:
Auditing the whole cast against the rule this wave just measured showed the rule
was stated too broadly. Terra's court dress says "circlet gone" at rung 2 and
"both gloves gone" at rung 3, and it lands at all five rungs in every arm at both
seeds - because those rungs still name a garment that IS present, "green gown with
a torn hem". The rungs that failed named only removals. So the test to apply to a
rung is not "does it contain a removal", it is "after the removals, is anything
still named".

The audit also found the state of the rest of the cast against this: TERRA is the
only character with a costumes map at all, and PIP's single wear ladder is
subtractive at all five rungs, which makes it the next one to look at.

entries.author: sechang11
entries.subject: TERRA is the reference character, and a costume is text before it is weights
entries.body:
Six agents built the full dossier for one cast member and every one of them was
told not to edit her card, so every one of them ended by saying the card now
disagrees with the evidence. This wave verifies their claims against the pixels,
answers the headline question, adds two measurements nobody ran, and closes the
disagreements.

VERIFIED ON THE BOX, NOT TAKEN ON TRUST. Six contact sheets opened across five
agents. The setting result is the clean win: v1 at 0.85 replaces a snow forest
with a featureless taupe void, v3 holds a real forest at the same seed and the
same strength - the "0.85 destroys the setting" finding was never about strength,
it was the uncaptioned taupe turnaround backdrop absorbed into the trigger. The
named-view octants produce a textbook V curve and the handedness collapse is real:
profile_l and profile_r both face screen-left. higgs_v3 really has no dynamics -
four registers, four identical waveforms. Eleven styles really do repaint her hair
red, and the same cells are the ones where the style made her small.

THE HEADLINE ANSWER IS A QUALIFIED YES, AND THE QUALIFIER IS THE INTERESTING PART.
The retrain fixed the court dress decisively and replicably: v1 with the danbooru
name in the prompt produces the canonical polka-dot bodice in every court cell at
both seeds, v3 produces a real green gown with gold embroidery and white gloves.
It did not fix imperial plate and it never could have fixed the field coat,
because those two were never weights problems.

TWO WRITING RULES, MEASURED RATHER THAN INFERRED. Two agents independently
diagnosed the field coat from the two rungs that already worked and neither tested
the fix. studio/_tools/field_fix.py renders the same five rungs with the shipped
text and with the gold dress taken out of levels 0 and 3, four arms, two seeds:

  1. NEVER NAME THE GARMENT A COSTUME EXISTS TO REPLACE. Level 0 read "heavy brown
     travelling coat OVER THE GOLD DRESS". The model renders nouns, so it rendered
     the gold dress and dropped the coat. Removing four words puts the coat on her
     in four arms out of four.

studio/_tools/damage_nouns.py then tested the same suspicion on the rungs the
armour collapses at, which are written the same way:

  2. WRITE DAMAGE AS A DAMAGED THING, NOT AS A MISSING THING. "one pauldron gone",
     "breastplate discarded" and "satchel gone" give the sampler nothing to draw,
     so it falls back on whatever the trigger and the tag already know - which is
     the default costume. The same state written as objects that are present
     brought real metal, a gauntlet and greaves back at plate rung 3 in both seeds
     and put the torn coat back on at field rung 3. Honest limit: plate rung 4 only
     recovers its tabard.

Both rules are on the card as costume_text_rule and both are expected to hold for
every character in this project. dossier.py already had a text-only check that
predicts exactly these failures without booking a GPU; it now fires on one rung
instead of three, and the one left is the terminal rung, where naming the default
costume underneath is deliberate.

THE CARD NOW SAYS WHAT THE RENDERS SHOW. costume_verdict no longer blames the
weights alone and keeps a paragraph saying what it used to say. costume_note no
longer claims damage is orthogonal to wardrobe - it is orthogonal for cloth and
destructive for structure. style_verdict carries the 250-cell sweep instead of a
five-style probe. status_note no longer says nothing has been rendered. New
view_verdict, frame_verdict, emotion_verdict, place_verdict and motion_verdict
move five sweeps' conclusions off tool-local prose and onto the card. Two
disagreements are left open on purpose and written up as identity_note: the
headpiece is a horned gold ornament and not the red ribbon the tags claim, and the
bodice colour flips seed to seed. Fixing either means a new sheet and a retrain,
not a tag edit.

lora_scan.py stops calling every trained character LoRA an orphan. A file has two
possible owners - the pickable library and a character card's lora key - and the
scanner only knew about one, so it has reported PROBLEMS FOUND since the first
character was trained. That is a boy-who-cried-wolf failure: a real orphan now
arrives in a list already known to be wrong and gets skipped. It separates the two,
still fails on a character card pointing at a missing file, and the negative
control was run.

Sizes: the character sweeps get the policy gallery/ and cast_proof/ already have.
Contact sheets, measurements.json and verdicts.json stay tracked because they are
what a claim rests on; the full-size cells behind them are regenerable from the
tool named in each sweep's docstring, and 600 MB per character would put this
repository past what a git host will take.

named-view octants produce a textbook V curve and the handedness collapse is real:
profile_l and profile_r both face screen-left. higgs_v3 really has no dynamics -
four registers, four identical waveforms. Eleven styles really do repaint her hair
red, and the same cells are the ones where the style made her small.

THE HEADLINE ANSWER IS A QUALIFIED YES, AND THE QUALIFIER IS THE INTERESTING PART.
The retrain fixed the court dress decisively and replicably: v1 with the danbooru
name in the prompt produces the canonical polka-dot bodice in every court cell at
both seeds, v3 produces a real green gown with gold embroidery and white gloves.
It did not fix imperial plate and it never could have fixed the field coat,
because those two were never weights problems.

diagnosed the field coat from the two rungs that already worked and neither tested
the fix. studio/_tools/field_fix.py renders the same five rungs with the shipped
text and with the gold dress taken out of levels 0 and 3, four arms, two seeds:

1. NEVER NAME THE GARMENT A COSTUME EXISTS TO REPLACE. Level 0 read "heavy brown
     travelling coat OVER THE GOLD DRESS". The model renders nouns, so it rendered
     the gold dress and dropped the coat. Removing four words puts the coat on her
     in four arms out of four.

studio/_tools/damage_nouns.py then tested the same suspicion on the rungs the
armour collapses at, which are written the same way:

2. WRITE DAMAGE AS A DAMAGED THING, NOT AS A MISSING THING. "one pauldron gone",

     so it falls back on whatever the trigger and the tag already know - which is
     the default costume. The same state written as objects that are present
     brought real metal, a gauntlet and greaves back at plate rung 3 in both seeds
     and put the torn coat back on at field rung 3. Honest limit: plate rung 4 only
     recovers its tabard.

predicts exactly these failures without booking a GPU; it now fires on one rung
instead of three, and the one left is the terminal rung, where naming the default
costume underneath is deliberate.

weights alone and keeps a paragraph saying what it used to say. costume_note no
longer claims damage is orthogonal to wardrobe - it is orthogonal for cloth and
destructive for structure. style_verdict carries the 250-cell sweep instead of a
five-style probe. status_note no longer says nothing has been rendered. New
view_verdict, frame_verdict, emotion_verdict, place_verdict and motion_verdict
move five sweeps' conclusions off tool-local prose and onto the card. Two
disagreements are left open on purpose and written up as identity_note: the
headpiece is a horned gold ornament and not the red ribbon the tags claim, and the
bodice colour flips seed to seed. Fixing either means a new sheet and a retrain,
not a tag edit.

lora_scan.py stops calling every trained character LoRA an orphan. A file has two
possible owners - the pickable library and a character card's lora key - and the
scanner only knew about one, so it has reported PROBLEMS FOUND since the first
character was trained. That is a boy-who-cried-wolf failure: a real orphan now
arrives in a list already known to be wrong and gets skipped. It separates the two,
still fails on a character card pointing at a missing file, and the negative
control was run.

Sizes: the character sweeps get the policy gallery/ and cast_proof/ already have.
Contact sheets, measurements.json and verdicts.json stay tracked because they are
what a claim rests on; the full-size cells behind them are regenerable from the
tool named in each sweep's docstring, and 600 MB per character would put this
repository past what a git host will take.

entries.author: sechang11
entries.subject: A photographic sheet is a casting decision, not a transcription
entries.body:
TERRA's first photographic sheet was cosplay: a green wig, a craft-felt cape,
upholstery-print fabric, shiny vinyl boots, flat frontal light against a grey wall.
Technically it matched her card exactly, which was the problem. qwen_sheet.py transcribed
her anime vocabulary straight into a photo prompt - gold dress, red cape, red boots - and
Qwen rendered precisely that.

Nobody films a drawing. They build it out of real material and light it. So the fix is
nouns, not adjectives, which is this project's rule applied one layer further out:

  MATERIAL  raw silk, wool, worn leather - not gold and red. Material is the single
            biggest tell between a costume and a wardrobe, and it is a noun, so it lands.
  LIGHT     a window camera-left with deep falloff, not flat frontal. Flat light is what
            makes a costume look like a costume.
  LENS      85mm at f/2, for the compression an audience reads as film.
  POSE      weight on one hip, three-quarter turn. Symmetry with limp arms is a passport.
  HAIR      named as dyed with visible roots. The words green hair on a photoreal model
            return a wig.

studio/_tools/photo_sheet_probe.py renders four treatments at one seed and keeps the
literal transcription as cell 1 so the comparison stays honest. Evidence at
studio/samples/cast/terra_photo_probe.jpg. Cell 2 is now her sheet; cell 4 is kept
separately as a face reference, being the better face but showing no costume.

Character cards may now carry photo_prose, and qwen_sheet.py prefers it. A card without
one still builds a sheet and now says plainly what it will get and how to fix it, rather
than shipping a wig and calling it a reference.

entries.author: sechang11
entries.subject: TERRA is a real cast member, and training a character teaches it its clothes
entries.body:
The LoRA beat the tag decisively. Two places the training set never contained, four
columns, one seed. The danbooru tag with no LoRA puts her tiny and dark in the far
distance with the face unreadable. At 0.5 she is properly framed and holds green hair,
red ribbon, red cape, gold dress and red boots across both places.

The column that decides it: with the danbooru name STRIPPED OUT of the prompt entirely,
she still comes back as Terra. The weights carry her, not the tag. She is a cast member
rather than a prompt trick and can be put in any scene like VIRO or NIKA.

0.85 collapsed snow_road's forest to a flat beige void, which confirms the NIKA finding
on a second character. The measured-safe strength generalises.

A NEW LIMIT, and it applies to every LoRA-backed character here. The wardrobe map works
at the prompt layer - court dress lands cleanly, green gown and circlet - but imperial
plate and field coat only partly land: a pauldron and a gauntlet appear and the gold dress
persists underneath. The LoRA was trained on sixteen views of ONE outfit, so the outfit is
encoded as part of the identity and a costume change fights the weights that make her her.
That is a property of how characters are trained, not a flaw in the costumes map.

Two styles hijack the composition rather than the medium: ukiyo_e put her inside an
ornamental arch and gothic_illustration shrank her to a kneeling figure across a wide
hall - the same frame-building behaviour the styles library recorded for art_nouveau and
illuminated_manuscript.

entries.author: sechang11
entries.subject: Characters get a wardrobe, and TERRA is built
entries.body:
TERRA is the first cast member with provenance=known_partial - the danbooru tag reaches
her palette and silhouette but the description-only control lands nearly as close, so she
got the same full build as an invented character. Sheet, 16-view turnaround, LoRA trained
in 10.5 minutes and landed in models/loras rather than the SaveLoRA output trap.

One thing caught at the sheet stage, which is the cheap place to catch it: the tag
"pointed ears" gave her full elf ears, which is not her design. A wrong noun trained into
a LoRA is permanent and would ride along in every later render, so the tag came out and
the sheet was re-rendered before anything downstream saw it.

WARDROBE. wear_tags looked like a wardrobe and was not - it is five DAMAGE LEVELS of one
outfit, so a character had exactly one costume for their whole existence and "the same
person, in armour" had nowhere to live. Cards may now carry a `costumes` map of NAMED
outfits, each with its own five levels, because damage is orthogonal to wardrobe: armour
dents the way a dress tears. wear_tags still means the default costume, so every existing
card and film is untouched.

compose.py resolves a `costume` selection, falls back to the default with a named warning
when the costume does not exist, and keeps the damage ladder intact inside each one -
verified: armour at 0/2/4 gives polished plate, then a dented pauldron and torn mail, then
the breastplate discarded and the left arm bound.

TERRA ships with four: traveller, imperial plate, court dress, field coat.

entries.author: sechang11
entries.subject: Can we cast a character the model already knows? A probe, and Terra as the worked example
entries.body:
Every cast member so far was invented here, so each costs a sheet, a turnaround and a LoRA
- about twenty minutes of GPU. A character out of an existing game is a different problem,
because animagine is trained on the danbooru corpus where well-known characters are tagged
by name. If the tag has mass she comes back from the tag alone, with no build at all, and
more consistently than a trained LoRA because she is in the base weights rather than
patched on top.

So the first question is never how do we build her. It is does the checkpoint already have
her. studio/_tools/known_char_probe.py answers that in four cells at one seed: the danbooru
form, the bare name, name plus description, and THE DESCRIPTION ALONE WITH NO NAME. That
last cell is the one a careless test omits. If the control looks like the named cells then
the name did nothing and the adjectives are carrying it - the governing rule applied to
character names. A name only counts as known if it beats its own description.

Terra Branford, measured on animagine at seed 9090: the bare name returns a BLONDE IN A
WHITE HOOD, not her. The danbooru form gets the green-blonde hair, red cape and an orb -
the orb is a noun the tag really does carry. But the description-only control lands nearly
as close, so the tag is thin. Verdict: partially known, not reliably known. She cannot be
cast from a name; the build is the same as any original character, and the name is worth
using to seed a better reference sheet.

Character cards now carry provenance - original, known_strong, known_partial or
known_absent - so the probe is never run twice and nobody assumes a famous name will just
work. All six existing cards are stamped original.

craft/KNOWN_CHARACTERS.md records the method, the Terra result, and the one thing worth
knowing before publishing rather than before rendering.

entries.author: sechang11
entries.subject: The reference sheet now follows the engine, which is the whole non-anime cast fix
entries.body:
Measured this session: the qwen edit path fed a character's ANIME sheet returned flat cel
illustration in 4 of 4 places, even with "waist-up photograph" in the prompt. Fed a
PHOTOGRAPHIC sheet of the same character - same prompt, same seeds, same graph apart from
which png node 8 loads - it returned a photograph in 4 of 4, with the laundromat,
snowfield, library and market street all intact and one recognisable person throughout.
A reference sheet imports its style as forcefully as its identity.

The two photographic sheets that proved it were written onto the cards and wired to
nothing, so no film could reach them. compile.py now picks sheet_photo when the film
renders on qwen and falls back to the anime sheet otherwise. Verified: a qwen film with
NIKA emits sheet_photo_nika.png, an anime film emits the anime sheets unchanged.

And nothing silently does nothing - a qwen film whose character has only an anime sheet
now warns, names the consequence, and gives the command that fixes it. Verified firing on
derby-qwen for VIRO.

The only compiled-film change is character_lora_weights gaining VIRO 0.5, which is the
motion arm's measured strength reaching the renderer rather than the old 0.85 default -
the strength that turned NIKA's sunlit field into a grey void.

entries.author: sechang11
entries.subject: Cast: a face that survives eight seconds of motion, and a sheet that survives the medium
entries.body:
Two questions a user would actually ask, both answered by rendering and looking:
can I trust a character in a moving shot, and can I put one in a non-anime style.

MOVING SHOTS - YES, AND THE CLOCK IS NOT WHAT COSTS YOU.
studio/_tools/cast_motion.py, 12 clips of VIRO across six places the training set
never held, one video seed throughout, plus a LoRA-dropped control and 8s
re-renders. Within a clip he holds for the full eight seconds tested: at f192 of
c1_walk_in_long the number 7, both gold ear studs, the two-tone hair and the amber
eyes are unchanged from the keyframe, and the drift curve is non-monotonic
(0/43/52/14/43/54/23/55/20) - hair breathing, not a face going. What ends a face is
the ACTION completing, at a fraction of the clip rather than a wall-clock second,
so doubling the clip roughly doubles the face time.

The structural fact that frames all of it: the character LoRA is NOT in the video
graph. short.py splices node 90 into the anime keyframe workflow only. Between
clips identity is the LoRA's job; within a clip it is entirely LTX's, and no card
field can help. Confirmed from source, not inferred - the control drifts no more
than the LoRA arm does, so the LoRA makes him a specific person and is not what
makes him stable.

VIRO's card gained lora_strength_measured 0.5, from the downward sweep his LoRA
card asked for and never got, and which compile.py already knows how to deliver.

NON-ANIME - YES FOR PHOTOGRAPHY, PARTLY FOR PAINT.
studio/_tools/cast_style.py, 82 cells. A reference sheet imports its style as
forcefully as its identity, and swapping the sheet is a complete fix: the anime
sheet returned cel illustration in 8 of 8 cells with "waist-up photograph" in the
prompt, and a photographic sheet returned a photograph in 8 of 8, same prompt, same
seeds, same graph apart from which PNG node 8 loads, with every scene intact. The
cost is fine markers only - NIKA's heterochromia reads in 2 of 4 photographic cells
against 4 of 4 on the anime path, while her scar and all of PIP's markers carry.

Also established, and it applies to every qwen graph on this box: THE NEGATIVE
PROMPT ON A 4-STEP QWEN WORKFLOW IS INERT. The Lightning LoRA forces cfg 1.0, so
there is no classifier-free guidance and the negative is never subtracted. Verified
again during review by differencing the two arms: 8 of 8 pairs byte-identical,
bounding box of the difference empty. Do not author one and do not blame one.

THREE CORRECTIONS MADE DURING REVIEW, all from re-reading the renders:

- NIKA's card claimed watercolour, ink_wash and oil_painting all land at IPAdapter
  0.0. Only ink_wash does. Its saturation collapses to 7.9 in the library against a
  control of 36.7; watercolour, oil_painting and oil_painterly all sit AT OR ABOVE
  their own control in both places, and looked at they are cel with different
  lighting. The IPAdapter-0.0 conclusion stands; the count of styles does not.
  The card also attributed market_street's hue run to the library. Both fixed.

- VIRO's card cited a white patch on his forehead as evidence for 0.50 over 0.85.
  It is not evidence: the same patch is plainly present in the strength 0.00
  control and in three 0.50 cells of between.png. It is a pipeline-wide artefact at
  every weight including zero. The 0.50 choice stands on the scene evidence, which
  read at full resolution is worse than recorded - at 0.85 all five subway posters
  collapse into the same flat teal panel carrying his own jersey number.

- VIRO's card said the 8s head turn loses the face by f168. At f168 it is a clean
  profile with the eye open and the gold ear stud legible. Frontal or three-quarter
  ends at f144 (75%); a usable profile runs to f168 (87%); the face is gone at f192.

STILL OPEN, AND NAMED SO NOBODY REDISCOVERS IT: sheet_photo is on the cards but
unwired - compile.py and short.py have no field for it, so nothing in the app picks
these sheets up yet. The motion library's measured bands did not transfer to new
keyframes and should not be quoted at a user until re-measured. And no photographic
keyframe has been pushed through the LTX pass.

entries.author: sechang11
entries.subject: A changelog in the app, generated from git rather than maintained by hand
entries.body:
/changelog reads studio/changelog.json, which studio/_tools/changelog.py builds from git
log. A changelog somebody has to remember to update is one that goes stale, and this
project already has enough places where a card claims something the pixels do not
support - so the history is the source.

It is unusually good source material here, because the commit bodies record what was
MEASURED rather than what was intended: what was rendered, what was looked at, and where
a claim turned out to be wrong. Those bodies are the interesting half, so the first
paragraph is always open and the rest is one click away.

Area tags are derived from the paths each commit touched rather than from words in the
subject, so a commit that edits studio/styles is tagged Styles whether or not it says so.
Filter buttons across the top; 57 changes over 13 areas at the time of writing.

Regenerate with: python3 studio/_tools/changelog.py

entries.author: sechang11
entries.subject: Motion: the films stop asking the video model to hold still
entries.body:
Every beat of every film carried one constant string, "Slow deliberate movement
only." - 29 beats, three films, the only assignment to motion in the compiler.
It was measured at 0.520 against an empty control's 0.614: not merely useless
but one of the stillest cells in an 81-clip sweep. For an app built to ask for
precise video, the single string the video model reads was asking for nothing.

It is gone. Motion now resolves through compose.resolve_motion() on a four-rung
ladder - an explicit @card, free text, a derivation from the author's own shot
line, or a measured hold - so the compiler, the wizard and the thumbnail
renderer answer the question in one place. 0 of 41 beats across four films
carry the constant now.

WHAT THE RENDER SHOWS. A 12-beat film was authored to walk all four rungs and
rendered end to end, then six beats were re-rendered with the retired constant
at the identical keyframe and seed. On the confetti beat the new string fills
an empty classroom with confetti while the constant leaves the room untouched
for the whole clip - and the constant DRIFTS MORE while showing less. That
pair is the whole wave in one image.

TWO THINGS THE EYE CAUGHT THAT THE NUMBER DID NOT. A completed hand-raise -
the hand rising to the face and holding, subject and framing intact - measures
0.863, inside the empty control's band. Ranking motion cards by the metric
would have discarded every performance beat; analyze_shots.motion() is a
frame-scale event detector and is blind to subject-scale action. Separately,
the sweep's claim that a spatial anchor rescues a dead mover FAILED TO
REPLICATE when run as a clean single cell: "The curtain lifts behind her."
does not lift the curtain on any of three seeds. The rule that survives is
about the mover, not the grammar - it must be free to travel and hard-edged.

CAMERAS AND TRANSITIONS NOW TELL THE TRUTH. dolly_zoom, orbit and rack_focus
emitted an empty filter chain and shipped output byte-identical to static;
all three now carry status unavailable and renders "none". short.py reports
any camera fx_chain() cannot render, which closes a wider hole than the three
roadmap moves - a TYPO was previously indistinguishable from a working move.
j_cut and l_cut are recorded as picture-identical by design, because their
content is audio and it is wired; smash is partial because its audio_drop has
no reader anywhere; match_cut now emits the reminder its card had promised.

A 34-card motion library was authored and measured at three seeds each, and
the honest yield is that 8 cards do what they say. The other 25 are negative
results, which is the point: each one would otherwise have shipped as a silent
no-op exactly like dolly_zoom.

THIS COMMIT ALSO FIXES two defects found while checking the above. Derived
motion had no subject-verb number agreement, so a plural mover shipped broken
grammar to the model - "Loose papers blows across the floor.", "Birds crosses
the frame.", and "They leaps forward" for a they/them character. For a project
whose governing rule is that the exact grammar is what was measured, that is a
defect in the one string that matters. Singulars that merely end in s are
preserved ("Broken glass slides across the floor."). And a weak card's second
verdict was never surfaced: hold_nobody's own verdict is a stillness number,
while the fact that the word "Nobody" DREW A PERSON into a shot authored "no
humans" sat unread in verdict_prior. The author now sees it, and is pointed at
hold_frame instead. All four films recompile byte-identically, so neither fix
changes an existing beat.

KNOWN AND NOT FIXED HERE. A derived motion copies the author's spatial anchor
without checking it is in the picture: a shot line reaching "toward the window
sill" over a keyframe with no window made LTX build one, turning night into
day. Free text can attach the motion to the wrong object - a named chair
stayed still while the shaft of light slid toward camera. Hallucinated
occupants are a model property, not a regression: the retired constant walked
a pair of legs into the same insert. serve.py's GROUPS omits "motions", so the
library is invisible in the app, and the scene-level camera grid still offers
the three dead moves - both are the cast wave's files and were left untouched.

entries.author: sechang11
entries.subject: Render the female-character negative fix, and correct the claim it was meant to confirm
entries.body:
The cast wave reported that workflows/22's shipped negative, which opens with 1girl,
girl, female, feminine, breasts, was a BLOCKER making a female character unrenderable -
the positive asking for a girl and the negative forbidding one on the same beat. The fix
in short.py _negative() was verified by assembling the ComfyUI graph and reading it back,
and against zero pixels.

Rendered now, at one seed, four cells. NIKA comes back an unmistakably female character
BOTH WITH AND WITHOUT the fix: white hair, heterochromia, blazer, side braid. The
contradiction is real and removing it is correct, but it did not stop the render.
Blocker was overstated. Contradiction worth removing is accurate.

The property that did matter holds: the male control had NOTHING dropped from its
negative in either cell, so the rule leaves every existing character's prompt untouched.

One correction to my own check. I compared the two male cells by md5 and reported the
rule as over-broad when they differed. That was the wrong instrument - the log shows both
male cells had identical prompts, and the byte difference is render nondeterminism across
a model reload, 7.8s versus 65.1s. The rule is not over-broad.

Also stopped a runaway gallery_gen.py --vary all --loop, PID 161380, which had held the
GPU at 100% for 17 hours and 22 minutes and blocked at least three agents across two
waves. Killed by PID, never by pattern, because a pattern kill here matches the ssh
wrapper and takes the session with it.

entries.author: sechang11
entries.subject: Cast: six characters, three trained faces, and the two wires that made the measurements reachable
entries.body:
Six character cards where there were three, three trained LoRAs where there was one, and a
cast page that re-checks every claim against the filesystem instead of trusting the card.

WHAT WAS MEASURED, by rendering and looking - not inferred

  base_tags works. NIKA renders an unambiguous teenage girl and PIP an unmistakable
  nine-year-old. They are the first non-male renders in this project, and the first cards
  to carry base_tags at all. Without it compose.py appends the module constant
  "male focus, mature male, masculine" to slot 2 of every anime prompt.

  A character LoRA drags its own training background's value and hue into every scene, and
  that is why the cost varies between characters. NIKA was trained on a dark blue-grey
  backdrop and at 0.85 her sunlit field collapses to a dark grey void with a strip of
  grass. PIP was trained on a light warm grey and at 0.85 the same scene merely pales.
  0.5 keeps the face and gives the scene back. Read studio/samples/cast/nika_sweep.jpg.

  A held prop survives a turnaround, and training improves it. Without the LoRA PIP's toy
  is a shapeless blob in one scene and a blue dolphin in another; at 0.5 it is an
  unmistakable green spiky dinosaur in both.

  The reference sheet through IPAdapter SUPPRESSES STYLE - the LoRA does not. At the
  shipping weight of 0.6, eight of nine styled cells are indistinguishable from the
  unstyled cell beside them: an ink_wash prompt carrying "monochrome, greyscale" returns a
  full-colour anime picture. Set IPAdapter to 0.0, leave the LoRA on, and all three styles
  land while the character still holds. Read studio/samples/cast_proof/viro_style.jpg.

  A stray highlight in a sheet becomes a permanent character trait, and this is now the
  SECOND time. PIP's sheet had white tufts at the crown; the turnaround amplified them into
  all 16 views and the LoRA learned white-over-orange hair his card never asked for. The
  chain is sheet -> turnaround -> LoRA and each stage trusts the last completely.

  A detail below the frame of the sheet cannot be trained in. PIP's odd red and green
  wellingtons are in all five wear rungs, his sheet is framed upper-body, and no strength
  recovers them.

  The qwen reference-sheet path holds identity across five unseen places at no cost to the
  scene, where the anime LoRA bleaches every scene toward its training backdrop. It imports
  its own medium in exchange: with an anime sheet every cell is an illustration however
  loudly the prompt says photograph. The lock generalises to a face with ZERO distinctive
  markers, which retires the previous doc's untested caveat.

TWO WIRES, which is what this commit adds on top of the wave

  THE MEASURED STRENGTH COULD NOT BE APPLIED. short.py read a single film-wide
  character_lora_weight defaulting to 0.85, and compile.py never emitted it - it was not a
  movie variable, not settable at any level, and absent from every compiled film. So every
  film rendered every character LoRA at exactly the strength measured to destroy NIKA's
  setting, while her card recorded 0.5 and could not reach the renderer. compile.py now
  emits character_lora_weights from each card, and short.py prefers it. Verified by
  assembling the real graph: node 90 comes back at 0.5 for NIKA, 0.85 for VIRO.

  A FEMALE CHARACTER COULD NOT RENDER THROUGH THE PRODUCT. workflow 22 ships a negative
  opening "1girl, girl, female, feminine, breasts" and short.py never wrote node 6 at all,
  so the renderer asked for a girl in the positive and forbade one in the negative on the
  same beat. Every image of NIKA in this wave was made with that negative replaced by hand.
  short.py now drops any negative clause whose every word also appears in the positive.
  Verified on the assembled graph: NIKA loses "1girl, girl, female"; VIRO and MANAGER come
  back byte-identical to the shipped workflow. NOT YET VERIFIED IN PIXELS - the box was
  queue-bound behind a 17-hour render loop and no film of hers has been rendered end to
  end. The first person to render her should look.

  The cast page had gone on printing "THERE IS NO TOOL FOR THIS YET" for a missing
  reference sheet while TWO working sheet tools shipped in this wave under names the probe
  did not know. Both are listed now, labelled by engine, because a sheet imports its style
  and which one you run is a decision about the film.

WHAT IS STILL BROKEN, recorded rather than papered over

  PIP needs "adult, mature male, muscular" pushed INTO the negative and no card field can
  express that; the renderer will not invent it. character_demo.py and lora_check.py are
  both male-hard-coded and cannot verify either new character. BRACK's canvas apron renders
  as blue denim dungarees in all 17 images, and "bald" beat "grey hair" so his horseshoe
  fringe never appeared. NIKA's sidecut never rendered at any strength. MANAGER gained
  round glasses that appear nowhere on his card. compose.py still tests the card field
  rather than the filesystem for both the sheet and the weights, so it will call a card
  fine that names a file that is not there - the cast page checks disk and disagrees.

SWEPT IN, and named rather than hidden: studio/compose.py and part of studio/compile.py
carry an in-flight motion wave's work that I did not author or verify, along with its tools
and samples. They are committed because the tree they form is the one that was verified to
compile, serve and pass check_refs, and splitting a page from its API across a commit
boundary is the mistake this wave already made once. 194 MB of regenerable full-size proof
cells are now gitignored, matching the policy already written into this file for stills;
the contact sheets that carry the findings stay tracked.

entries.author: sechang11
entries.subject: Video: 225 clips where there were 24, and a metric that ranks two of them backwards
entries.body:
Before this wave every mp4 in the project was ffmpeg over a still. No camera,
motion, transition or style value had ever been through a video model, and all
130 style cards carried a works_for VIDEO claim that was inferred and never
rendered. This wave rendered 201 new clips and looked at them.

WHAT THE RENDERS SETTLED

The standing prediction - "flat, high-contrast idioms hold through i2v; fine
grain and dot fields boil" - is falsified. All nine illustration styles held
their idiom for 8s, including the three the library named as worst cases.
manga_screentone, whose card predicted itself "the WORST case in this set",
has flat detail octiles and boils less than the no-style control, at three
separate seeds. The axis that predicts survival is illustration vs photograph,
not flat vs textured - though engine and idiom are perfectly confounded in this
library, so that split is not yet attributable to either cause.

Three of eleven camera moves are silent no-ops. dolly_zoom, orbit and
rack_focus have no branch in short.py fx_chain(), so the filter chain comes out
empty and the clip passes through untouched - their mp4s share the MD5 of
static.mp4 exactly. The wizard has been offering three moves that do nothing.

The one string the video model reads is the one nobody libraried. compile.py
gives every beat of every compiled film the constant "Slow deliberate movement
only.", which measures indistinguishable from an empty prompt at all three
seeds tried. The rule is sharper than nouns-vs-adjectives: large moving objects
land, fine atmospheric nouns do not.

Asked of the model rather than cropped after, rack_focus renders a hanging
chain into centre frame - asked for an optical quality, it drew a noun. orbit
produces the only genuine 3D camera move in the project. tilt_d tilts up.

LTX stays the default. Wan holds faces better and does not drift, but it
ignores the pipeline instruction "slow deliberate movement only", costs 4x, and
emits no audio. LTX applies an unrequested push-in that the pull move in
fx_chain then fights.

WHAT THIS COMMIT CORRECTS

_control.json claimed "Both keep the subject and both keep the shot." That is
false, and it is the card every other style is read against. Opening both
detail strips: the anime control subject is specified looking at viewer, and
from f110 her hair covers her face with her eyes closed through f192, while
the qwen control keeps face, gaze and identity stable for the full 8s. The
anime clip scores the best detail in the sweep (1.007) and the qwen clip the
decaying one (0.870) - exactly backwards from what a viewer sees, because
flying hair IS high-band amplitude. detail can stay high while the subject is
destroyed. Recorded on the card.

analyze_shots.py read YDIF with a digits-and-dot character class, which matches
8.87784e-05 as 8.87784. Verified on a still encoded to h264: a frozen clip
measured 1.31 instead of 0.001, a 1300x overstatement. The DEAD score is
secs*(1/motion), so a dead shot scored LOW and never surfaced in --worst. The
one failure the tool exists to catch was the one it could not see.

The engine-split means went stale when pointillism was reclassified from anime
to qwen after the sweep ran. Recomputed: 8 anime 0.946, 5 qwen 0.754, not 9 at
0.953 and 4 at 0.690. The finding survives; its size was overstated by about 40
percent. The pointillism card still described in the present tense a mismatch
that had since been fixed on it, and its published clip was rendered on the
other engine - now labelled as a stale sample.

LORAS.md said accelerators run at "1.0, exactly". Rendering settled it: at 1.0
the LTX distill grows orange particle blobs absent from both the keyframe and
the 0.5 render. strength_range narrowed to [0.5, 0.5] and the doc no longer
contradicts a card marked ready.

/video shows all 225 clips as 128 comparison cards, side by side, with recipes
imported live from the tools that made them rather than retyped.

WHAT IS STILL ONLY CLAIMED

Nobody has watched a single clip play at frame rate, on this wave or any
previous one. Every verdict here rests on frame strips plus the metric. No
audio has ever been listened to, though LTX generated a track on all 201 new
clips. Most style verdicts are n=1, and the seed replicates showed photographic
styles swing enormously across seeds while illustration ones do not - so those
per-card photographic verdicts are one draw from a wide distribution.

separate seeds. The axis that predicts survival is illustration vs photograph,
not flat vs textured - though engine and idiom are perfectly confounded in this
library, so that split is not yet attributable to either cause.

Three of eleven camera moves are silent no-ops. dolly_zoom, orbit and
rack_focus have no branch in short.py fx_chain(), so the filter chain comes out
empty and the clip passes through untouched - their mp4s share the MD5 of
static.mp4 exactly. The wizard has been offering three moves that do nothing.

The one string the video model reads is the one nobody libraried. compile.py
gives every beat of every compiled film the constant "Slow deliberate movement
only.", which measures indistinguishable from an empty prompt at all three
seeds tried. The rule is sharper than nouns-vs-adjectives: large moving objects
land, fine atmospheric nouns do not.

Asked of the model rather than cropped after, rack_focus renders a hanging
chain into centre frame - asked for an optical quality, it drew a noun. orbit
produces the only genuine 3D camera move in the project. tilt_d tilts up.

LTX stays the default. Wan holds faces better and does not drift, but it
ignores the pipeline instruction "slow deliberate movement only", costs 4x, and
emits no audio. LTX applies an unrequested push-in that the pull move in
fx_chain then fights.
WHAT THIS COMMIT CORRECTS

_control.json claimed "Both keep the subject and both keep the shot." That is
false, and it is the card every other style is read against. Opening both
detail strips: the anime control subject is specified looking at viewer, and
from f110 her hair covers her face with her eyes closed through f192, while
the qwen control keeps face, gaze and identity stable for the full 8s. The
anime clip scores the best detail in the sweep (1.007) and the qwen clip the
decaying one (0.870) - exactly backwards from what a viewer sees, because
flying hair IS high-band amplitude. detail can stay high while the subject is
destroyed. Recorded on the card.

analyze_shots.py read YDIF with a digits-and-dot character class, which matches
8.87784e-05 as 8.87784. Verified on a still encoded to h264: a frozen clip
measured 1.31 instead of 0.001, a 1300x overstatement. The DEAD score is
secs*(1/motion), so a dead shot scored LOW and never surfaced in --worst. The
one failure the tool exists to catch was the one it could not see.

The engine-split means went stale when pointillism was reclassified from anime
to qwen after the sweep ran. Recomputed: 8 anime 0.946, 5 qwen 0.754, not 9 at
0.953 and 4 at 0.690. The finding survives; its size was overstated by about 40
percent. The pointillism card still described in the present tense a mismatch
that had since been fixed on it, and its published clip was rendered on the
other engine - now labelled as a stale sample.

the LTX distill grows orange particle blobs absent from both the keyframe and
the 0.5 render. strength_range narrowed to [0.5, 0.5] and the doc no longer
contradicts a card marked ready.

/video shows all 225 clips as 128 comparison cards, side by side, with recipes
imported live from the tools that made them rather than retyped.
WHAT IS STILL ONLY CLAIMED

Nobody has watched a single clip play at frame rate, on this wave or any
previous one. Every verdict here rests on frame strips plus the metric. No
audio has ever been listened to, though LTX generated a track on all 201 new
clips. Most style verdicts are n=1, and the seed replicates showed photographic
styles swing enormously across seeds while illustration ones do not - so those
per-card photographic verdicts are one draw from a wide distribution.

entries.author: sechang11
entries.subject: Templates: 62 styled cards, and the two silent defaults that were undoing them
entries.body:
The wizard opens on a gallery of templates, and all 20 of them set no style and no
engine. They predate the styles library, so every one fell through to the same anime
default while 130 measured styles, 64 places and a whole second photographic engine sat
unreachable from the front door. Four authors wrote 62 new cards in parallel to close
that. This change lands them, and fixes two things that would have quietly cancelled the
work out.

WHAT LANDED
62 cards, every one setting a style card and every one naming a real place card rather
than free text, which no existing template does. 16 photographic, 16 anime idiom, 15
illustration, 15 genre world. 59 distinct styles over 57 of the 64 places. Engine spread
goes from 20 of 20 anime to 45 anime and 17 qwen - the photographic engine is now
reachable from the gallery for the first time.

THE TWO DEFAULTS
1. The wizard state carries a free HOUSE-TAGS string, default "modern sports anime, cel
   shading, cinematic", appended verbatim to every prompt in the film. applyTemplate
   wrote every key of the template into state but never touched it, so it survived a
   template pick. Compiled, not guessed: the watercolour card came out ending
   "wet-on-wet, bleeding colours, pale palette, soft edges, paper texture, modern sports
   anime, cel shading, cinematic". Cel shading is the opposite of wet-on-wet and it was
   landing AFTER the style card's own tags, in all 62. That is the exact fault these
   cards were written to cure, reappearing one layer down. applyTemplate now clears the
   house tags when the template names a style card; templates that name none keep them,
   so the original 20 are unaffected.

2. check_refs.py declared rules for templates.look and templates.style but read them at
   the card root, while a template carries them inside sets. It validated nothing. Proof:
   62 cards carrying over a thousand ids landed and the count it printed stayed at exactly
   636. It now descends into sets, covers the whole layer stack plus the per-shot shot and
   camera ids, and treats an id-shaped place that does not resolve as a typo to eyeball -
   the same dual-purpose handling movies.style already had. 636 references checked
   becomes 1925, still 0 dangling. Negative-tested: it catches the invented look name
   "warm" that this file was written for in the first place.

VALIDATION, ALL CPU-ONLY
Every card parses, carries all 11 root keys, and has an id matching its filename. 1925
references resolved against the live directories, 0 dangling. Every style used is
status=ready; none is compose=inert or compose=injects. All 62 resolved through
POST /api/compose across 301 shots: 0 errors, 22 clean, 40 warning-only. 8 cards spanning
all four waves expanded to .movie exactly as the wizard emits and compiled through
compile.py at rc=0.

Dedupe: no two cards share a style and place, and no two share a place and shot shape.
Of 45150 shot-pair comparisons, 9 exceeded 0.60 similarity and 8 of those are the framing
grammar and the place nouns the place cards require. One was a real copy - the master shot
of the two bridge templates was the same sentence at 0.742 - and it is restaged. Nothing
was merged or dropped: every close pair differs on style, which is the axis the gallery
exists to spread, so deleting a card would have removed coverage this job was created to
add.

status is normalised to untested across all 62. Four authors had split 47 to 15 on a field
nothing consumes, and untested is the value that is true for all of them.

NOTHING HAS BEEN RENDERED
The GPU was held for a video job and no image or video job was submitted at any point.
None of the 62 has a thumbnail - the 20 originals have one each and these have zero, so
they will show as blank tiles until a render pass runs. What is proved is that the layer
stack resolves, the engine routes, and the film compiles. It is NOT proved that any of
these produces a good picture: every aesthetic claim on these cards is read off the style
cards' verdict fields and compose.py's static resolver, and behaviour of a compose=replaces
style over a dense place card is measured for only 4 of 16 such styles at a single seed
while 11 of these cards use one. The next step is a render pass, and it should look at
those 11 first.

entries.author: sechang11
entries.subject: A home page you can steer from, a Places page, and the ability to LOOK at any of it
entries.body:
Three things.

/places. Sixty-four settings, 192 renders, and until now no page to see them. Each card
shows BOTH engine renders side by side, because a place carries danbooru tags and prose
precisely so the two models can each be fed what they want, and seeing one render tells
you half of what the place is. Each card also shows its noun density, which is the
measured predictor of whether a style will overwrite the location: a locker room with
eleven concrete nouns held its ground against four styles that flattened a three-noun
free-text scene entirely.

The home page is now a hub rather than a link list. It opens with the layer stack drawn
in order, because style picking the engine is the one thing a new user has to understand
before anything else makes sense. Every library carries an honesty ledger - measured,
weak, unavailable, untested - so the state of the project is legible at a glance instead
of buried in card fields.

And studio/_tools/shot.py, which is the reason the two pages above could be judged rather
than guessed at. Nobody on this project had ever LOOKED at most of these pages: four
agents tried and reported failure, because the box has no Xvfb and Firefox headless dies
on RenderCompositorSWGL. The fix was pip-installing playwright chromium into the user
cache, which needs no root. It waits on domcontentloaded rather than networkidle - these
grids lazy-load dozens of thumbnails and networkidle never fires - and it reports JS
errors, because a screenshot that hides a broken page is worse than no screenshot.

page_snapshot.py is a fallback for viewing a page where the server cannot be reached: it
freezes the API responses into the file and stubs fetch, leaving the page's own code
untouched.

entries.subject: wizard: actually send the user's own LoRA pick to the resolver
entries.body:
composeBody() returned eight keys and omitted style_lora and style_strength, both of
which the wizard already tracked. So picking a LoRA in the UI changed the picture and
nothing else - no base-model gate, no conflict, no reason line. The resolver had been
ready since the last commit; the page simply never asked.

Both fields are now sent, with "none" preserved as a real sentinel meaning explicitly
off, distinct from null meaning let the style card decide.

Verified against the live endpoint on three states: an explicit pick at 1.2 resolves
active with the file and strength; "none" resolves inactive; and passing nothing still
lets a style card's own recommendation apply.

be EXECUTED. The branch logic was reimplemented exactly and exercised against the real
/api/compose, and the page serves 200 with the new keys present, but that the JS parses
is checked only by brace balance. Worth a browser pass.

entries.subject: LoRA examples: a strength ladder, because a LoRA image without its control proves nothing
entries.body:
studio/_tools/lora_examples.py renders every image LoRA as a ladder at a fixed seed and
fixed subject - 0.0 alongside the working strengths. The 0.0 cell is the evidence. A
single with-the-LoRA image cannot tell you what the LoRA did.

What the ladders show, seen not inferred:

illustration-1.0-qwen-image: at 0.6 near-inert. At 1.0 it swaps the SUBJECT - a European
adult woman becomes an East Asian child - while the image stays photographic. Only at 1.5
does the medium become a painted illustration. I earlier reported 1.0 as genuine painted
illustration; that was read off a small contact-sheet cell and was wrong.

qwen_image_modern_anime_lora: inert at 1.0 without its trigger, a real anime illustration
at 1.0 and 1.5 WITH the trigger phrase. The trigger is load-bearing.

qwen_image_2512_storybook_anime_lora: essentially inert at 0.0, 0.8 and 1.2 - three near
identical photographs. This is the LoRA that has been silently applied at 0.8 to every
qwen keyframe this project has ever rendered, so the standing bug was real but harmless.

Both style LoRAs carry a strong subject prior and will fight an authored cast. A reference
sheet through Qwen-Image-Edit corrects it.

The tool prints the 15 LoRAs it does NOT cover, each with its reason - edit LoRAs need a
source image, video LoRAs need a clip, Flux has no checkpoint on this box, and one is a
language model. A tool that quietly renders 5 of 20 and prints done is how a gap becomes
invisible.

entries.author: sechang11
entries.subject: LoRA library, an authored style-LoRA slot, and how a face is held on qwen
entries.body:
Twenty installed LoRA files were reachable only by typing a filename into a
workflow. Nothing recorded what any of them was trained on, and a LoRA on the
wrong base does not fail - it attaches to nothing and the picture just quietly
comes out unchanged. This adds the card library, the resolver layer that gates
on base model, a page to read it, and the renders that settle what a style LoRA
and a reference sheet actually do.

THE STANDING BUG IS FIXED. workflows/13 node 7 was a live LoraLoaderModelOnly
holding qwen_image_2512_storybook_anime_lora at strength 0.8, overridden only by
a film setting style_lora, which no film did. Every qwen keyframe and every qwen
reference sheet this project ever made carried an unauthored style delta. Node 7
now ships at 0.0 and short.py sets it explicitly on both keyframe paths, so a
stale workflow file cannot bring it back. Measured at a fixed seed, this is not
a grade shift: 16.2 dB PSNR and 64 percent of pixels moving on a stadium prompt,
milder but still real on a tunnel prompt. Old keyframes and sheets are not
reproducible from today, which is the intended fix and worth knowing.

That LoRA also has a trigger phrase read straight out of the safetensors header,
storybook anime illustration, and no prompt ever contained it. Rendered proof it
is load-bearing: at 1.0 untriggered a plain subject stays a photograph; the same
call with the phrase appended returns a flat anime illustration.

studio/loras/ 20 cards, one per file, each carrying base_model, kind, trigger,
strength, strength_range, status and a verdict. Three say ready, one weak, one
unavailable, fifteen say untested and mean it. studio/_tools/lora_scan.py checks
every card against the file bytes and fails on a status of ready with no verdict.
serve.py grows /api/loras and studio/loras.html renders it, recomputing the
on-disk check per request rather than trusting the card.

compose.resolve_style_lora() is the new layer, under style, exported and used by
both compile.py and the wizard. Base model decides whether the file is handed to
the renderer at all; a mismatch is an error with a fix line, not a note. Across
5000 randomised calls there are no exceptions and not one LoRA reported active on
a base it cannot attach to.

entries.subject: check_refs: movies.style is dual-purpose, stop calling it dangling
entries.body:
The first version flagged all three films for setting style to free text. That was the
checker being wrong, not the films. A .movie style value resolves as a card when it names
one - and the compiler takes the engine from that card - but when it does not resolve it
is legacy house-style tags appended to the prompt on the anime path. derby-ep1 relies on
the second meaning and compiles correctly: cel shading and modern sports anime are both
in its first beat. derby-qwen deliberately does NOT get them, because anime tags fed to
the prose path is a measured failure.

So the rule is dropped, and replaced with a narrower hint: report a style value only when
it LOOKS like an id (no spaces, no commas) and still does not resolve, which is a typo
rather than a choice.

entries.subject: Layer composition: one resolver, and the renders that corrected it
entries.body:
Adds studio/compose.py, a pure non-raising resolver that answers one question:
given a style, place, character, look, wear, lighting and weather, what
actually reaches the model, and what fights what. compile.py and the web app
now both go through it, so an authored .movie and the wizard share a single
code path instead of two drifting ones.

WHAT IS NEW
  studio/compose.py     the resolver: engine derivation, prompt assembly for
                        both engines, and 36 cross-layer conflict checks
  studio/styles.html    browsable styles library, 130 cards, each shown on the
                        engine its own card routes to
  /api/styles           serves the cards with per-engine examples
  /api/compose          delegates to the resolver, never reimplements it
  wizard step 3         the layer stack drawn as nested bands, with live
                        conflicts and per-layer prompt attribution
  studio/_tools/layer_demo.py   renders a layer stack, so a claim about
                        composition can be checked against a picture
  craft/STYLE_AND_LAYERS.md     what compose, status and engine mean

WHAT THE RENDERS CHANGED
compose=replaces is CONDITIONAL on how many nouns the place brings, and the
warning said otherwise. sheet_C.jpg puts shojo_soft, wasteland, cottagecore
and solarpunk over place: locker_room, and all four left the room standing -
lockers, benches, tiled floor and end window intact, recoloured but not
replaced. sheet_G.jpg isolates why: the style verdicts were measured against
three loose tags, and against that thin setting the same styles DO delete the
location. A place card carrying eleven concrete nouns wins. This is the
project governing rule doing what it says - nouns win. The conflict now scales
with place density and points at the sheet.

The cross-engine LoRA constraint is now proved from pixels rather than
reasoning. sheet_E.jpg force-loads the trained character LoRA into the qwen
graph and the result is byte-identical to the pass without it, every key
reporting not loaded, while on anime the same file transforms the image.

FIXES FOUND BY ATTACKING THE RESOLVER AND BY LOOKING AT THE PAGES
  compile.py named the wrong value on an unknown engine: it printed the film
    engine var, which is None when the bad value came off the style card, so
    the author was told to go fix a line they never wrote
  lighting and weather error codes were truncated to lightin and weathe by a
    blind plural chop, so no consumer matched them and the wizard could not
    colour the band that was actually wrong
  a place id that does not exist sailed into the prompt as a literal token
    with no conflict at all; now caught, with a near match suggested
  a typo'd style id was described as the no-style control, contradicting the
    error printed next to it
  three look cards naming an object (firelight, day_for_night, blockbuster)
    were missing from the place-noun table, so look: firelight over a place
    card drew an actual campfire in it
  film-level warnings dropped their fix sentence and then suppressed the
    per-beat copy that would have carried it
  /api/compose returned the full text of every card it touched, 52% of the
    payload, on a request the wizard fires every 180ms while you type
  HEAD answered 404 on every route while GET returned 200, because the class
    inherited the SimpleHTTPRequestHandler do_HEAD, which resolves against the
    process working directory instead of the route table
  the gallery put 48 audio artifacts in an img tag; they now get a player

NOT FIXED, AND KNOWN
  scripts/short.py still has no negative input on either keyframe workflow, so
    every style negative_add is assembled and then thrown away. The sample
    images in the styles library were rendered WITH it and a real film renders
    without, so the library evidence does not match what the pipeline produces.
  workflows/13_qwen_t2i_styled.json node 7 loads an unauthored style LoRA at
    strength 0.8 on every qwen render. Measured as real but mild.
  compose=injects and compose=inert, 28 of the 130 cards, have not been
    rendered at all. The injects warning is the one the wizard shouts loudest
    and nothing here says whether it holds.
  Nothing has been checked as video. Every temporal-stability warning is
    inferred from prose, not measured.

entries.subject: Styles: 130 cards, every one judged from its own render
entries.body:
A style decides which model can render it at all, so `style` is authored at film level
and `engine` is derived from it. Wave one shipped 46 of 64 cards marked ready without a
single render; all were downgraded and re-measured, and 27 of 64 turned out to be routed
to the wrong engine.

Measured, not assumed:

- Qwen-Image cannot be steered off photography by prompt at ANY cfg. 20 steps at cfg 4.0
  with the Lightning LoRA disabled and "painting, illustration" in the negative still
  returned a photograph. The agents predicted negatives would bite once off cfg 1.0; that
  is refuted. Painterly styles belong on the SDXL path, which is the ILLUSTRATION engine,
  not merely the anime one - it does watercolour, ukiyo-e and oil paint beautifully.

- A style whose NAME contains an object noun gets the object drawn, usually into the
  subject's hands: graffiti -> spray can, airbrush_70s -> airbrush, pulp_cover ->
  paperback, persian_miniature -> golden tray, tattoo_flash -> face tattoos,
  food_photography -> plate of food, wildlife_photo -> a fox. This is the project's
  governing rule - the model renders nouns, not adjectives - biting in the style layer.

New field `compose`, which the wizard's layer stacking needs:
  safe     re-renders the scene in a new idiom          86
  replaces re-renders AND overrides the setting         16
  injects  the name's noun becomes a prop in frame      20
  inert    no visible change from the control            8

Also added studio/checkpoints/qwen_image_2512.json - 42 styles route to qwen and the
checkpoints library described only the two anime SDXLs.

impossible without a post-process (it works directly), cubism was called weak (the
background genuinely fractures), iyashikei was called weak (it lands), voxel was routed to
qwen (it needs the illustration engine).

entries.author: sechang11
entries.subject: Style comes first, and it chooses the engine
entries.body:
An image is always in some style, and that choice decides which model can render it at
all. The two families here want opposite prompt formats, and asking the anime checkpoint
for photorealism is a contradiction it cannot resolve. So `style` is now authored at
movie level and `engine` is DERIVED from it - the author picks how it should look, not
which model does what.

  style: cel_anime_90s   -> engine anime, animagine, danbooru tags
  style: photorealistic  -> engine qwen, Qwen-Image, prose

An explicit engine still wins, because a style card can be wrong and someone who has
looked at the output should be able to override it. When the two disagree the compiler
says so rather than silently picking one. A style marked `weak` warns at compile time.

The style's marks reach the prompt on whichever path it routed to: its danbooru tags join
the tag string on the anime path, its prose joins the sentence on the qwen path.

NAMING. `styles` is distinct from `looks`, which in this project already means something
specific - a deterministic ffmpeg colour grade applied AFTER generation. Style is how it
is drawn; look is how it is graded. The style cards say so where the two could be
confused.

A BUG CAUGHT BEFORE IT SHIPPED: the qwen branch had a local `style = v["tags"]` inside the
beat loop. Adding a film-level `style` card of the same name would have rebound it on the
first beat and clobbered it for every beat after. Renamed to house_tags.

Verified: a film setting only `style: _probe` (engine qwen) compiled to keyframe_engine
qwen with the style prose in the beat prompt, without naming an engine anywhere.

64 style cards are being authored now across anime, photographic, painted and graphic
idioms - each stating which engine it needs and, honestly, where it cannot be done well
on this box at all.

entries.subject: 64 places, rendered on both engines - and the first non-anime content
entries.body:
studio/places/ has been declared in compile.py since the format was written and has been
EMPTY the whole time, so every scene typed its setting as free text. That is how
"rooftop" in one scene became a different building from "roof" in another.

64 places across nature, urban, interior, industrial, historical and fantastical.
Validated before installing: 0 problems, every suits_looks resolves to a real look, and
NO MOOD WORDS anywhere in tags or prose - checked for eerie/foreboding/atmospheric and
found none, which is the rule that matters since the model renders nouns.

Two things the agents corrected in my brief, both fair:
  - I said the looks library was 7. It is 25. They read the actual directory and paired
    against real ids - sodium for streetlight, fluorescent for subway and factory, neon

entries.author: sechang11
entries.subject: Character demo across settings, and what the LoRA actually contributes
entries.body:
character_demo.py puts one character in eight settings none of which were in the
training set. The turnaround proves the re-poser works; it does not prove the character
survives being put somewhere new, which is the only thing anyone wants from a cast.

Ran it both ways, because without the control "looks consistent" is an impression:

  WITHOUT LoRA  the teal jersey, the number 7 and the curly ponytail are ALREADY there.
                The tag string carries most of the identity on its own - which is the
                same finding as the IPAdapter weight sweep that measured the character
                "already recognisable at ZERO".
  WITH LoRA     adds what the tags cannot say: the two-tone blonde-and-brown hair, a
                more defined and older face, a broader build.

So a character LoRA is not what makes a character recognisable. It captures the part of
a likeness that words do not reach. Worth knowing before spending ten minutes of GPU per
character.

A COST I did not expect and would have missed without the control: the no-LoRA settings
are BETTER. Neon street renders as a real rainy alley without the LoRA and as an interior
with a window with it; sky palace keeps its birds and clouds without and goes generic
with. At strength 0.85 the LoRA is pulling attention away from the setting. Lower
strengths are worth sweeping - character_lora_weight already exists per film for exactly
this.

Also: the demo runs --engine qwen for the non-anime path, where the LoRA does NOT apply,
since it is a delta on animagine weights. That pass is a genuine test of how far the
written description alone carries a character.
